title: Interpersonal Relationships and Health Behaviors Among Systems-Involved Youth
text:
Close relationships with caregivers and peers are critical to risk and resilience patterns among
systems-involved youth; however, almost no work has incorporated the role of romantic
relationships among these youth. Across relationships, innovation is necessary to capture
naturalistic interpersonal processes and identify targets for interventions to promote healthy
close relationships. This study will support the R15 goals of creating a research environment by
providing rich training opportunities for undergraduate students in technology mediated
communication data, ecological momentary assessment, self-report data, and clinical interviews
to understand both the daily and distal associations between adolescents’ interpersonal
processes and relationship health, sexual health, and psychosocial adjustment.

title: Multi-scale functional dissection and modeling of regulatory variation associated with human traits
text:
Hundreds of thousands of genomic regions have been associated with human traits and diseases, yet in few
instances do we know the identity of the exact causal mutation nor the molecular mechanism behind its
function. This proposal aims develop new tools to mutagenize gene regulatory elements in the genome and
build a catalog of epigenetic and transcriptional phenotypes from over 300,000 mutations. This catalog will be
used to augment advanced machine learning models to better understand the underlying rules of how variants
function, as to better predict the impact of individual mutations linked to human health and disease.

title: Overcoming CAR T cell resistance by tumor-restricted IL-12 driven anti-tumor immunity
text:
This proposal focuses on strategies to leverage engineered, tumor-localized delivery of the cytokine
interleukin-12 (IL-12) and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapies for solid tumors to improve T cell
trafficking to disease sites, remodel the tumor immune microenvironment, and safely eradicate tumors with
variable tumor antigen expression or loss. The major outcomes of this project will be an advanced
understanding of the mechanisms by which IL-12 functionally interacts with CAR T cells and endogenous
immunity as well as the nomination of safe and rational approaches for clinical therapeutic translation.

title: Investigating the role of Alzheimer's disease familial mutations in neuromuscular physiology
text:
We propose constructing a two-organ microphysiological system composed of human cells for both sensory and
motor segments of the reflex arc to study the effects of Alzheimer’s disease on the peripheral nervous system.
We will establish clinically relevent functional models for AD by treating healthy systems with Aβ42 and tau
oligomers in addition to motor and sensory systems composed of AD mutant iPSC MN-based NMJ systems to
better understand the effects beyond the well studied systems in the brain.

title: Heritable immunization of the white-footed mouse reservoir of Lyme disease
text:
RFA-AI-19-037
The Mice Against Ticks project seeks to prevent new cases of Lyme disease by heritably
immunizing the white-footed mice that are most responsible for infecting ticks. Engineering
local mouse populations to carry naturally occurring immunity elements isolated from other
mice in a reversible fashion may be the safest and most minimal intervention capable of
preventing Lyme disease for many decades. Our open and community-guided approach has
generated considerable interest and apparent enthusiasm from the residents of Nantucket and
Martha’s Vineyard, suggesting that it may be widely adopted to protect communities suffering
from Lyme disease throughout the Northeast and Upper Midwest.

title: A Longitudinal Multimodal Risk Prediction Platform for Personalized Breast Cancer Screening
text:
Breast cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related death in women, and current risk
models fail to accurately identify many women at elevated risk. This project will develop an
AI-powered risk assessment tool that leverages longitudinal mammographic and clinical data to
provide more precise, individualized predictions of near-term breast cancer development. By
improving early detection and optimizing screening strategies, this innovation has the potential
to reduce mortality, decrease unnecessary imaging, and advance access to personalized breast
health care.

title: Innovative implementation of artificial intelligence techniques for enhanced management of aortic abdominal aneurysms
text:
Abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) are life-threatening conditions influenced by intraluminal thrombus (ILT),
which contributes to arterial wall degradation and increases the risk of rupture. This study will explore the link
between hemodynamics, ILT formation, and AAA rupture by integrating computational modeling, machine
learning-based data analysis, and deep learning-based image processing techniques. It aims to enhance risk
assessment and clinical management strategies for AAA patients, bridge crucial gaps in understanding disease
progression, and pave the way for improved patient outcomes.

title: Postoperative Delirium- Unmasking of Pre-existing Deficits, or De Novo Injury to the Brain
text:
More than 19 million older Americans (age >65) undergo surgery each year, and up to 40% develop
postoperative delirium (POD), a syndrome of fluctuating changes in attention and consciousness that leads to
an increased risk for postoperative mortality and Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD). This
project will study delirium mechanisms and determine the extent to which delirium reflects an unmasking of
latent/prodromal brain dysfunction (such as amyloid or tau pathology, or neuroinflammation) vs the extent to
which delirium represents a de novo injury to the brain that accelerates the development of cognitive decline and
ADRD. The proposed research has significant public health implications, as it will allow the PI to expand his
efforts in mentoring junior investigators in patient-oriented research on delirium and ADRD mechanisms, which
will eventually lead to the development of novel drugs targets to prevent and to treat POD and ADRD.

title: Honing Precision Medicine for Type 2 Diabetes in the Veteran Population
text:
With 25% of US veterans affected by Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) and at substantial risk for disease complications,
this proposal seeks to enhance their healthcare through personalized medicine. By integrating genetic,
lifestyle, dietary, and methylation data, we aim to identify those at highest risk, generate leads for therapeutic
modalities, and understand basic mechanisms. Our broad objectives are to create systems with tools for earlier
detection and improved outcomes for high-risk veterans, ultimately reducing the burden on the VA health
system and improving veteran quality of life.

title: Defining the role of germline Daam2 variant R414W in familial glioma
text:
Familial glioma represents an understudied subset of glioma with marked hereditary predisposition. Recent
discovery and preliminary findings of germline variants in Daam2, a critical regulator in glial development and
cytoskeletal structure, have uncovered a potential risk mutation capable of promoting glioma growth. This
proposal aims to functionally characterize the role of germline Daam2 variant R414W in glioma susceptibility,
growth, and progression, ultimately defining its impact on glioma development.

title: Novel HCV vaccine antigens and nanoparticles
text: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infects 1-2% of the world population and poses a significant threat to public health. Recent studies have identified a panel of broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) and their genetic preferences. The crystal structures of various HCV E2 constructs in complex with bnAbs and non-nAbs provide a structural basis for rational vaccine design. In Project 2 of this P01 proposal, we will combine structural optimization of HCV antigens, nanoparticle engineering, in vivo assessment, and next-generation sequencing (NGS) of B-cell repertoires to assist in rational design of HCV vaccines that can elicit a bnAb response. The Specific Aims in this project are: (1) To develop vaccine antigens to target multidonor class antibody responses. The major virus neutralizing site, the E2 neutralizing face (E2 NF), is a well-known multidonor class antibody target on HCV. E2 NF is conformationally flexible and is surrounded and protected by immunodominant variable loops and N-glycans. The antigenic surface at and around E2 NF will be optimized by computational modeling and mutagenesis scanning to “lock” E2 NF into desired neutralizing conformations. A rigid E2 NF, together with modifications to improve protein folding and to minimize the decoy effect of immunodominant epitopes, should improve the immunogenicity of vaccine antigens and as a result elicit multidonor class bnAbs to the conserved neutralizing epitopes. (2) To develop E1E2-based vaccine antigens. In addition to E2 NF, the native E1E2 complex also present other conserved bnAb epitopes. We will apply scanning mutagenesis to the interface of E1 and E2 ectodomains and design novel E1 and E2 fusion constructs to improve the stability and production of the soluble E1E2 complex for the elicitation of bnAbs targeting the quaternary structure of the complex. (3) To develop self-assembling antigen-presenting nanoparticle vaccines. The engineered E2 and E1E2 complex will be fused with the scaffold proteins of different nanoparticle platforms to identify a platform optimal for the multimeric display of HCV antigens to the immune system. Based on our preliminary data, this strategy will greatly improve the immunogenicity of vaccine antigens and elicit a rapid and potent nAb response. (4) To evaluate immunogenicity and antibody responses of vaccine candidates in the mouse and non-human primate (NHP) rhesus macaque models. The engineered E2, E1E2 antigens and nanoparticles will first be studied in mice to confirm their immunogenicity in vivo and their ability to elicit antibodies that can bind and neutralize HCV. The antigens and nanoparticles with the best properties in vitro and in mice will be studied further using the NHP model. We have recently shown that rhesus macaques react to E1E2 immunization in a manner highly reminiscent to that used by humans and develop bnAbs against E2 NF with genetic similarity to human bnAbs. Here, we will immunize NHPs, identify bnAbs, and perform repertoire NGS to evaluate selected antigen designs. The outcome of Project 2 would be a set of well-characterized HCV vaccine candidates.

title: Effects of adolescent social isolation on glial dysfunction and social behavior in adulthood
text:
Adolescence is a critical developmental stage during which individuals are especially vulnerable to social stress
that may alter behavior and increase psychiatric disorder risk later in life. Understanding the developmental
impact of social stress is crucial for advancing our knowledge of the neural mechanisms underlying dysfunction.
This proposal will investigate how adolescent social isolation stress induces microglial pruning of astrocytes,
altering astrocyte-mediated regulation of neural circuits that govern social behavior.

title: Reawakening cardiomyocyte proliferation from structural mediated quiescence
text:
This R01 project will address the synergy between Hippo/Yap and Wnt/b-catenin signaling in cardiomyocyte
proliferation in adult mice and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. Myocardial
infarction (MI) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality world-wide, and patients with MI often progress to
chronic heart failure, requiring heart transplantation or mechanical support devices to maintain survival. By
leveraging the synergy between Yap and Wnt signaling to induce MI border zone-specific proliferation of
cardiomyocytes, this project seeks to understand the mechanistic basis of cardiomyocyte proliferation in the
setting of myocardial injury to enable the development of future MI therapies.

title: Multiplexed reporter platforms for probing the bile acid- nuclear receptor interactome
text:
Bile acids (BAs) are core gastrointestinal (GI) metabolites with dual functions in lipid absorption and cell signaling.
Nuclear receptors (NRs) – a large family of ligand-regulated transcription factors – are a primary source of host
BA receptors in the GI tract, including in immune cells, yet only a fraction of the putative BA-NR ‘interactome’
has been explored because gold-standard reporter assays used to identify NR ligands are tedious and
singleplex. This proposal seeks to use, and build new, multiplex NR reporter systems capable of mapping global
interactions between physiologically defined mouse BA pools and all 48 NRs, with an eye toward streamlining
and expanding NR research by us and others.

title: Reprogramming organismal lifespan through modulation of neuropeptides
text:
Aging is the number one risk factor for debilitating diseases such as neurodegeneration. The fundamental
question that I will answer in this proposed research program is whether neuropeptides are key regulators of the
pace of aging and lifespan. My findings will change the way we think about the regulation of whole-body aging
and provide a tunable node within aging pathways to extend healthy lifespan.

title: Novel Integrative Analysis of Microbiome and Host Genetics in Childhood Asthma Research
text:
Childhood asthma is a major public health issue, with significant long-term impacts on children's
health and development. Within the context of the largest and most geographically diverse
microbiome and host genetics datasets from the Children’s Allergy and Asthma Data Repository
(CADRE), this proposal aims to develop novel statistical methods to enable robust and
comprehensive understanding of the interplay between microbiome and host genetics and their
implications for childhood asthma. This effort paves the way for developing new microbiome-
based strategies for asthma treatment and management.

title: Engineering Adeno-associated virus vectors for the in vivo generation of CAR T cells targeting HIV B cell reservoirs
text:
Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) remains a major global health challenge, with over 40 million people
affected worldwide. This project will develop and test adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based tools that enable safe
and efficient in vivo generation of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells targeting HIV infected cells, addressing
key limitations of current therapies such as the high cost of ex vivo cell manipulation and the need for lifelong
antiretroviral treatment. By establishing technologies that can direct precise, durable, and T cell-specific gene
delivery, this work will lay the foundation for future strategies aimed at achieving a functional cure for HIV.

title: Leveraging membrane Env liposome vaccine design to elicit multi-target cross-neutralization of HIV
text:
A vaccine for HIV/AIDS is needed which can induce antibodies that protect against all strains of
HIV. We will test a vaccine platform in monkeys that presents the whole HIV spike instead of
part of the spike and combine it with state-of-the-art delivery and design approaches to elicit
potent antibody responses against two key regions on HIV’s spikes.

title: SCH: Synergizing Topological Deep Learning and Spatio-Temporal Causal Inference to Unpack Health
text: The proposed research supports the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS) mission to discover how the environment affects people to promote healthier lives. The work will contribute to the NIEHS strategic plan for "Data Science and Big Data" by developing innovative data science and data-driven approaches overcoming analytical challenges in the data analysis of health drivers from national geospatial datasets and public health records, including multimodality, confounding, and spatial misalignment.

title: Frontiers in measuring and simulating molecular structures and processes.
text:
The proposed work would push the limits of methods for analyzing biomolecular structures
through both experimental measurements and computational simulation, overcoming the
limitations of existing methods used for studying biological processes driving health conditions
and developing drugs to treat these conditions.
The work would also correct flaws in the statistical methodology ubiquitously used in biological
and medical research and evaluation of treatments and drugs.
